question: What is the definition of a 'factory' under Section 2(m) of the Factories Act, 1948, and what are the worker thresholds that trigger its applicability?
answer: Under Section 2(m) of the Factories Act, 1948, a 'factory' means any premises where 10 or more workers are employed with the aid of power in a manufacturing process, or 20 or more workers are employed without the aid of power in a manufacturing process.

question: Under the Chhattisgarh Shops and Establishments Act, what are the key compliance requirements regarding registration, working hours, and weekly off for commercial establishments?
answer: Registration is required for establishments employing 10 or more persons (or as notified). Maximum working hours: 9 hours per day and 48 hours per week. Overtime is permissible up to prescribed limits with double wages. A mandatory weekly off of one day must be provided. Annual leave is as per Act provisions (e.g., one day per 20 days worked). The registration certificate must be displayed at the establishment premises, and records/registers for attendance, wages, and leave must be maintained. Non-registration attracts a fine as prescribed under the Act.

question: What are the penalties for contravention of hazardous process provisions (Sections 41A-41H) under Section 96A of the Factories Act 1948, and how do they differ from the general penalty under Section 92?
answer: Section 96A provides imprisonment up to 7 years with fine for contravention of hazardous process provisions; if contravention continues after conviction, an additional imprisonment of up to 3 years may be imposed. In contrast, the general penalty under Section 92 provides imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs. 1 lakh or both, with minimum fines of Rs. 25,000 if death resulted and Rs. 5,000 if serious bodily injury resulted. For repeat offences under Section 94, imprisonment increases to 3 years and fine to Rs. 2 lakh.

question: How many industries are declared to involve hazardous processes under the First Schedule of the Factories Act, 1948, and what specific legal provisions (Sections 41A through 41H) are triggered by this classification?
answer: 29 industries are declared hazardous under the First Schedule. The classification triggers: Section 41A (appointment of Site Appraisal Committee for initial location), Section 41B (compulsory disclosure of information by occupier to workers and public), Section 41C (specific responsibility of occupier), Section 41D (workers' right to warn about imminent danger), Section 41E (emergency standards where none exist), Section 41F (permissible limits of exposure to chemical/toxic substances per Second Schedule), Section 41G (workers' participation in safety management), and Section 41H (power of Central Government to appoint inquiry committee).
source_document: List of Industries involving hazardous processes _ DGFASLI, Mumbai, Ministry of Labour, Government of India_.pdf

question: Under the Chhattisgarh Factory Rules 1962, what are the alarm and automatic shutdown thresholds for flammable substance concentrations in ovens and driers (Rule 73A), and what are the explosion panel specifications?
answer: The safe dilution level is when flammable substance concentration is at or below 25% of the Lower Explosive Limit (LEL). The alarm must activate at 50% of LEL, and automatic shutdown must occur at 60% of LEL. Explosion panels must have an area of at least 2,200 sq cm per cubic metre of oven volume, and panels must be designed to release at 0.25 kg/sq cm internal pressure.

question: What does the Chartered Engineer Certificate (Appendix-4, Rule 6) under the CG Industrial Development Policy certify, and what is the maximum allowable investment rate for shed/building construction?
answer: The Chartered Engineer Certificate has two parts. Part A (Plant & Machinery): The Chartered Engineer visits the plant site and certifies the installation and commissioning of machinery, recording investment before expansion, during expansion, and total after expansion. Plant & machinery is defined to include main manufacturing machines, tools, jigs, dies, moulds, plus GST and transportation charges paid on machinery. Part B (Civil Work): Certifies completion of civil construction, capturing area (sq ft), rate per sq ft, and amount for factory building, warehouse, administrative building, labour duty room, and security guard post. The maximum allowable investment for shed/building construction is Rs. 1,000 per square foot. The certificate must be issued on the Chartered Engineer's letterhead only.

question: Under the CG Factory Rules 1962, what is the composition, tenure, and meeting frequency of a Safety Committee (Rule 73I), and in which types of factories is it mandatory?
answer: A Safety Committee is mandatory in: factories with 250+ workers ordinarily employed, factories carrying on dangerous operations under Section 87, and factories carrying on hazardous processes under Section 2(cb). Composition: management representatives include a senior official (Chairman), Safety Officer (Secretary), Factory Medical Officer, and production/maintenance/purchase representatives; workers' representatives are elected by workers. Tenure: 2 years. Minimum meetings: once every quarter. Minutes must be recorded and produced to the Inspector on demand.

question: What documents are required for a Factory Plan Approval (Form 1-A) application in Chhattisgarh, and what is the timeline for certificate issuance?
answer: Required documents: (1) Land ownership proof (Khasra/Khatoni), (2) NOC from local bodies, (3) Ownership/company proof (MOA/AOA), (4) List of Directors, (5) Manufacturing process description and flowchart, (6) Architectural/engineering drawings per Rule 3A(1) in 3 sets, (7) Consent to Establish from SPCB for Water Pollution, (8) Consent to Establish for Air Pollution, (9) Onsite Emergency Plan (mandatory for hazardous industry factories). Certificate issuance: within 30 days of application. Total application closure period: 90 days.

question: What is the factory registration/renewal fee under Schedule B for a factory with 501-1000 workers in Chhattisgarh, and what is the fee escalation rule?
answer: The fee under Schedule B for 501-1000 workers is Rs. 14,400. The fee escalation rule provides for a 30% increase every 3 years from 1 January 2014, rounded to the nearest multiple of Rs. 100.

question: How is the Variable Dearness Allowance (VDA) for beedi manufacturing workers in Chhattisgarh calculated, and what was the total effective wage per 1,000 beedis for beedi rollers from 01.10.2022?
answer: VDA is calculated based on the average All India Consumer Price Index (AICPI, base 1960=100) for July-June preceding the effective date. The formula: VDA = 1 paise per AICPI point rise per 1,000 beedis. For 2022-23: average AICPI was 8,256, base index was 6,321, rise = 1,935 points, so VDA = Rs. 19.35 per 1,000 beedis. Total wage per 1,000 beedis: Basic Rs. 96.24 + VDA Rs. 19.35 + Leave with Salary Rs. 5.78 = Rs. 121.37 total wages. Including bonus (Rs. 10.11) and employer PF (Rs. 12.14), gross total = Rs. 143.62.

question: What is the validity period of an Environmental Clearance (EC) for (a) river valley projects, (b) mining projects, and (c) all other projects under the EIA Notification 2006?
answer: (a) River valley projects: 10 years; (b) Mining projects: project life as estimated by EAC/SEAC, with a maximum of 30 years; (c) All other projects and activities: 5 years. An extension of a maximum additional 5 years may be granted on application made within the validity period.

question: Under the EIA Notification 2006, what are the four stages of the Environmental Clearance process, and what are the key timelines for each stage?
answer: Stage 1 - Screening: Only for Category B projects; SEAC determines if EIA is required (B1 = EIA needed, B2 = no EIA). Stage 2 - Scoping: Terms of Reference (TOR) must be conveyed within 60 days of receipt of Form 1; if not conveyed, applicant's proposed TOR is deemed final. Stage 3 - Public Consultation: Public hearing must be conducted by SPCB within 45 days of request; if SPCB fails, another agency gets a further 45 days; Summary EIA must be placed on website within 7 days of written request. Stage 4 - Appraisal: EAC/SEAC must appraise within 60 days of receiving final EIA report; recommendations placed before authority within next 15 days; authority must convey decision within 45 days of recommendations (total 105 days from final EIA receipt).

question: What is the scope of stamp duty exemption available under the CG Industrial Development Policy, and what types of documents and transactions does it cover?
answer: Full 100% stamp duty exemption is provided on execution of documents related to land, shed, and building purchase or lease for industrial purposes. It covers both purchase deeds and lease/tenancy deeds. Applicable to: new industrial units and expansion/diversification/substitution/modernization of existing units. No upper monetary limit is specified - it is a blanket exemption for qualifying industrial transactions. The exemption is claimed at the time of execution of the deed at the Sub-Registrar office. The unit must hold valid registration/acknowledgement under the applicable Industrial Policy and the land/building must be used for industrial purposes. Additionally, under the Logistics Policy 2025, stamp duty exemption also applies to loan-advance documents executed within 3 years of bank sanction date, and to purchase/sale of closed/sick industries.

question: How is electricity duty exemption calculated for expansion or diversification of an existing industrial unit under the CG Industrial Development Policy, and what is the exemption period?
answer: The electricity duty exemption period is 12 years from the date of commencement of commercial production. For expansion or diversification of existing units, the exemption is proportionate - calculated based on the ratio of additional investment in plant and machinery for expansion to the total investment (existing + expansion) in plant and machinery. For example, if existing P&M investment is Rs. 10 crore and expansion P&M is Rs. 5 crore, the proportionate exemption applies to 5/15 = 33.33% of electricity duty. For phased production, the proportionate ratio may be calculated per the time limits in Annexure-1 Para 17 of the policy, and the exemption period runs from the first production date after expansion/diversification.

question: What is the standard maximum storage period for hazardous waste under the HWM Rules 2016, and how did the 2024 Amendment modify storage periods for small generators?
answer: The standard maximum storage period is 90 days (Rule 8). The 2024 Amendment (9th Amendment, G.S.R. 177(E), 12 March 2024) split small generators into two sub-categories: generators producing 5 to 10 tonnes per annum get an extended storage of up to 180 days of annual capacity, while generators producing less than 5 tonnes per annum get an extended storage of up to 365 days (full year) of annual capacity. Previously, all generators up to 10 TPA were allowed 180 days.

question: Describe the 7-copy colour-coded manifest system for hazardous waste transportation under the HWM Rules 2016 (Form 10).
answer: The manifest has 7 colour-coded copies: Copy 1 (White) - Sender forwards to SPCB; Copy 2 (Yellow) - Retained by sender after transporter signs; Copy 3 (Pink) - Retained by receiver; Copy 4 (Orange) - Given to transporter by receiver; Copy 5 (Green) - Sent by receiver to receiver's SPCB; Copy 6 (Blue) - Sent by receiver back to sender; Copy 7 (Grey) - Sent by receiver to sender's SPCB, only applicable if sender is in another State (inter-state transport). The transporter cannot accept waste without signed copies 3-7.

question: What are the reimbursement rates for patent expenses and export certification expenses under the CG Industrial Development Policy's IP incentive scheme?
answer: Patent expense reimbursement: 100% of expenses incurred in obtaining patent certificates from Indian or foreign patent offices. International export certification: 50% reimbursement of the application fee, with a maximum of Rs. 15 lakh per product and a maximum of 10 products per unit. A critical condition is that the unit must demonstrate commercial exports of Rs. 50 crore or more per product to claim export certification reimbursement. Quality certification expenses (ISO-9000, ISO-14000, ISO-18000, BIS, ZED etc.) and technology acquisition costs are also covered under this scheme, with the annual maximum across all such grants capped at 2% of eligible fixed capital investment.

question: What are the key timelines for hazardous waste authorisation under the HWM Rules 2016: application deadline, SPCB processing time, validity, renewal application timing, and annual return deadline?
answer: Application deadline: within 60 days from date of publication of the rules. SPCB processing time: 120 days from receipt of complete application. Validity of authorisation: 5 years subject to conditions. Renewal application: can be made 3 months before expiry. Annual return (Form 4): filed to SPCB on or before 30th June following the financial year.

question: What is the Cumulative Pollution Index (PI) formula under the CPCB 2025 revised classification methodology, and what are the PI thresholds for each category (Red, Orange, Green, White)?
answer: The PI formula is: PI = i_max + (100 - i_max) x (i2 + i3) / 200, where i_max is the highest of the three pollutant group scores (PI_W for water, PI_A for air, PI_H for waste) and i2, i3 are the remaining two scores. Category thresholds: Red: PI >= 80; Orange: 55 <= PI < 80; Green: 25 <= PI < 55; White: PI < 25. Blue category uses the same PI calculation but is designated for Essential Environmental Services (EES) for domestic waste.
source_document: Red Orange Green & White List of CPCB 12.02.2025.pdf

question: What is the Consent to Operate (CTO) validity and inspection frequency for Red, Orange, Green, and Blue category industries under the CPCB 2025 classification?
answer: CTO validity: Red - up to 5 years; Orange - up to 10 years; Green - up to 15 years; Blue - category PI-based validity plus an additional 2 years as incentive. Inspection frequency: Red - at least once every 6 months; Orange - at least once every year; Green - at least once every 2 years; Common facilities and 17 specific categories - once every 3 months.
source_document: Red Orange Green & White List of CPCB 12.02.2025.pdf

question: What are the criteria for startup recognition under the Chhattisgarh Startup Policy, and what is the composition and role of the State-Level Startup Committee?
answer: Startup recognition criteria: the entity must be registered for less than 10 years (per DPIIT norms), and its turnover must not exceed Rs. 100 crore in any financial year. The entity must be registered under the Companies Act 2013, LLP Act, or Partnership Act. The State-Level Startup Committee is constituted to oversee startup promotion activities. It has the power to: review and approve/reject startup applications, grant recognition certificates, and disburse incentives. Applications are filed online through the designated portal, and approved startups receive a recognition certificate enabling access to policy benefits. The committee meets at prescribed frequency with quorum requirements.

question: What are the particulate matter (PM) emission limits prescribed by CECB for existing industries versus new/expansion units in critically polluted areas of Chhattisgarh?
answer: For existing industries, the stringent PM emission limit is 50 mg/Nm3. For new and expansion units, the PM limit is even stricter at 30 mg/Nm3 (which is 60% of existing flue gas and process emission standards). Additionally, large and medium Red category industries must install and commission Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) connected with CECB/CPCB servers.
source_document: new compliance list for orange and red.pdf

question: What are the key changes introduced by the 2024 HWM Amendment (9th Amendment) regarding EPR certificate pricing, polysiloxanes, and deposition centers?
answer: EPR certificates: CPCB fixes highest price at 100% and lowest price at 30% of the environmental compensation for non-fulfilment of EPR under Rule 39; exchange prices must fall between these limits. Polysiloxanes: post-industrial/pre-consumer polysiloxanes were moved from the prohibited import list (Schedule VI) to the permissible import/export list (Schedule III Part B). Deposition centers: A new definition was added (Rule 3, Clause 22A) for centers specified under Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 for domestic hazardous waste collection; they must obtain SPCB authorisation, maintain records in Form 3, and file annual returns in Form 4.

question: What are the enterprise size classifications under the Chhattisgarh Industrial Development Policy 2024-30 based on plant and machinery investment, and how does the policy classification differ from the general MSME classification?
answer: Under the CG Industrial Development Policy 2024-30: Micro - up to Rs. 1 crore; Small - up to Rs. 10 crore; Medium - up to Rs. 50 crore; Large - exceeding Rs. 50 crore. The key difference is that for purposes of this policy, classification is based ONLY on plant and machinery investment, not on annual turnover. The general MSME classification under the MSME Development Act uses both investment AND turnover thresholds (e.g., Micro: investment up to Rs. 1 crore AND turnover up to Rs. 5 crore).

question: What is the definition of a 'Women Entrepreneur' under the CG Industrial Development Policy 2024-30, and what special employment condition applies?
answer: A Women Entrepreneur is defined as: a state domicile female entrepreneur; or a partnership firm with minimum 51% women partners; or a company with 51% shareholding by women; or a cooperative with 51% women members. In each category, minimum 50% women employees must be maintained across managerial, skilled, and unskilled cadres (category-wise). If the owner is a woman, she is not counted in any labour category for this calculation.

question: What are the minimum requirements for a Residential Sports Academy and a Private Training Centre under the CG Service Sector Investment Promotion Rules 2025, and what is the appeal fee structure?
answer: Residential Sports Academy: Must provide intensive training in minimum 1 Olympic/National level sport, with accommodation for minimum 20 players. Fixed capital investment includes land, sports infrastructure, gym, swimming pool, yoga/fitness room, hostel, and mess. Private Training Centre (in Textile, Apparel, Footwear, Toys, Furniture sectors): Must train minimum 300 trainees per year, with adequate laboratory, workshop, resource centre, and certified trainers. For appeals: against any order of Commissioner/Director Industries or State Level Committee, appeal lies to State Minister of Commerce & Industry within 45 days. Appeal fee: Rs. 5,000 (general) or Rs. 2,500 for SC/ST, disabled, Naxal-affected, and surrendered Naxalites. The State Level Committee requires a quorum of 4 members.

question: What key financial incentive changes were introduced in the first amendment (Policy_Amend_1) to the CG Industrial Development Policy 2024-30?
answer: Key changes: (1) Net SGST reimbursement up to 100% of fixed capital investment over a defined period; (2) Fixed Capital Investment Subsidy at 35% rate across multiple investment slabs; (3) Electricity duty exemption for 12 years from commercial production date; (4) Interest subsidy of 50% of interest paid or 6% per annum (whichever lower) for 5 years with annual cap of Rs. 20 crore; (5) Full stamp duty exemption on land/shed/building purchase or lease deeds; (6) 50% registration fee reimbursement; (7) 50% land use diversion charge exemption up to 50 acres; (8) 50% new electricity connection charge reimbursement (excluding security deposit); (9) Employment generation subsidy of 20% of wages for CG domicile employees earning up to Rs. 50,000/month for 5 years (max 7 years from first commercial production), requiring 50+ permanent jobs. The option between Net SGST and Capital Subsidy is irrevocable and must be submitted with an affidavit.

question: What is the VIKALP scheme under the CG Industrial Development Policy, and what are the two tracks available to industrial units?
answer: VIKALP (meaning 'Alternative/Option') requires industrial units to make a one-time, irrevocable election between two incentive tracks: (a) Net SGST (State GST) Reimbursement Track - reimbursement of net SGST paid for up to 7-12 years depending on unit category, up to 100% of fixed capital investment; or (b) Fixed Capital Investment Subsidy Track - 35% of fixed capital investment with slab-based maximum caps. The option letter must be submitted with an affidavit in prescribed format before the first SGST return filing or first subsidy claim, whichever is earlier. Once submitted, the choice cannot be changed.

question: Under the CG Margin Money Grant Rules 2024, how is the grant disbursed to the unit, and what happens to the margin money grant after the unit is established?
answer: After the bank issues a loan sanction order, the bank demands the grant from the District Trade and Industry Centre (DTIC). The DTIC sends the grant to the bank via RTGS, which is credited to the unit's loan account (not given as cash or to a current account). The bank distributes the margin money proportionally in the same ratio as loan disbursement tranches. Budget for SC/ST entrepreneurs comes from the Tribal Special Component Plan/Adivasi Sub-Plan scheme. After the unit is established and commences commercial production, the margin money grant is adjusted against other incentive claims - specifically against the Fixed Capital Investment Subsidy, Interest Subsidy, or Net SGST reimbursement claims. Recovery, if needed, is at 12% per annum simple interest (notably lower than the 12.5% rate in other subsidy schemes).

question: For a unit doing modernization under the CG Capital Subsidy Rules, what are the eligibility conditions regarding minimum investment and machinery age?
answer: The unit must invest a minimum of 125% of its own existing plant and machinery investment for the modernization to qualify. The machinery being replaced must be at least 7 years old. If the modernization results in a 10% increase in total employment, the unit is eligible for 50% of the permanent capital investment subsidy up to the policy ceiling. The unit must inform the competent authority before starting the modernization process and must complete it by 31 March 2030.

question: What is the maximum project cost, grant percentage, and key eligibility conditions for the Margin Money subsidy under the CG Industrial Development Policy?
answer: Maximum project cost: Rs. 10 crore. Grant: 25% of the industrial unit's capital cost, subject to a maximum of Rs. 100 lakhs (Rs. 1 crore). Key eligibility: only state domicile entrepreneurs from specific categories (women, SC/ST, retired soldiers, retired Agniveer, Naxal-affected, disabled/Divyang) proposing new Micro and Small enterprises. The entrepreneur must arrange minimum 5% of project cost as margin money from own sources. No appeal fee is charged for margin money subsidy appeals, unlike other schemes.

question: What interest subsidy is available under the CG Industrial Development Policy 2024-30, and what is the annual cap?
answer: 50% of interest paid on term loans for plant and machinery, or 6% per annum, whichever is lower, for a period of 5 years from the date of commencement of commercial production. The annual cap is Rs. 20 crore. For thrust sector micro and small enterprises, the rate is 40% of interest paid or 5% rate (whichever lower) for 5 years, with an annual cap of Rs. 5 crore.

question: What is the standard recovery interest rate applied across all subsidy schemes under the CG Industrial Development Policy, and is there any exception?
answer: The standard recovery interest rate is 12.5% per annum simple interest, recoverable as land revenue arrears. This rate applies across the Capital Subsidy, Employment Subsidy, EPF Reimbursement, Transport Subsidy, Export Certificate Reimbursement, Water/Energy Efficiency, Clinical Trial, Net SGST Reimbursement, and Project Report Grant rules. The exception is the Margin Money subsidy, which specifies a recovery rate of 12% per annum simple interest.

question: What percentage of EPF employer's contribution is reimbursed under the CG Industrial Development Policy, for how long, and what is the annual cap?
answer: 75% of the EPF employer's contribution for Chhattisgarh state domicile employees is reimbursed. Duration: up to 5 financial years. Annual cap: 2% of eligible fixed capital investment per annum. Important condition: if the same employees also receive EPF reimbursement from any other Central/State government/board/institution, those employees are not eligible under this scheme.

question: How is transport subsidy calculated for export-oriented units under the CG Industrial Development Policy, and what are the maximum annual limits?
answer: Transport subsidy is calculated as 50% of actual transport expenditure (excluding government charges and taxes) from the manufacturing site to seaport or airport for export purposes, OR 2% of FOB (Free on Board) value of the exported product, whichever is less. Maximum annual cap: Rs. 50 lakhs per year for general units. SC/ST entrepreneurs receive a higher maximum of Rs. 60 lakhs per year. Duration: up to 5 years. Transport through intermediaries is not eligible.

question: What is the minimum per-product annual export value required to be eligible for export certification reimbursement, and what are the reimbursement limits?
answer: The unit must demonstrate per-product annual business exports of minimum Rs. 50 crore. The reimbursement covers 50% of application fees for international export certification, with a maximum of Rs. 15 lakh per product and a maximum of 10 products per unit. This scheme is available only to large enterprises under Chapter S (special product categories) that commenced commercial production after 01 November 2024.

question: What are the mandatory qualifications for water and energy audit bodies under the CG Water and Energy Efficiency Reimbursement Rules?
answer: For water audits, the auditing body must be on the list of auditors issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti (specifically the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation). For energy audits, the auditing body must be on the list issued by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, Government of India. Audits conducted by non-listed bodies are not eligible for reimbursement.

question: What unique features distinguish the Clinical Trial Expense Reimbursement Rules from other subsidy rules under the CG Industrial Development Policy?
answer: Three key unique features: (1) Application window is 18 months (vs. 6 months for most other schemes); (2) Eligibility is restricted to only large enterprises in the pharmaceutical sector (Chapter S-1), making it the most narrowly targeted subsidy; (3) CDSCO (Central Drugs Standard Control Organization) authorization/permission letter is a mandatory document. Eligible expenses include application fee, license fee, technical consultancy, patent fee, and other expenses related to clinical trials.

question: What is the employment multiplier for Fixed Capital Investment Subsidy introduced in the CG Industrial Development Policy amendment, and what are the multiplier values at each tier?
answer: Para 12.4(c) introduces employment-linked multipliers that increase the subsidy amount based on the number of employees: 100 employees: 1.1x multiplier; 200 employees: 1.2x; 500 employees: 1.3x; 700 employees: 1.4x; 1,000 employees: 1.5x. This means a unit with 1,000 employees effectively gets 50% more subsidy than the base rate.

question: What are the eligibility criteria and key incentives for Global Capability Centers (GCCs) under the CG Industrial Development Policy amendment?
answer: GCCs are defined as wholly owned subsidiaries of MNCs performing back-office, CoE, R&D, financial management, analytics, HR, and IT functions. Two levels: Level-1 GCC: Fixed Capital Investment Rs. 10-50 crore OR minimum 250 employees; Advance GCC: Investment above Rs. 50 crore OR minimum 500 employees. Key incentives: Capital Investment Subsidy (35%), Electricity Duty Exemption (12 years), full Stamp Duty exemption, Payroll Subsidy (20% of salary to CG domicile employees, max Rs. 2,00,000/employee/month, 10% of FCI annual cap), Operational Expenditure Subsidy (20% of opex for lease rent/internet/bandwidth/cloud, 2% of FCI annual cap), and Skill Development (50% of training cost or Rs. 50,000/employee, whichever lower).

question: What is the Udyam Aakanksha certificate, what is its validity period, and what are the fee amounts for each enterprise category?
answer: Udyam Aakanksha is a Certificate of Intent issued via the CG Commerce and Industry Department portal, serving as proposed registration for industrial investment promotion and industrial land allotment. Validity: 5 years from date of issuance (previously 2-year validity certificates were also extended to 5 years). Fees: Micro - Rs. 1,000; Small - Rs. 5,000; Medium - Rs. 10,000; Large - Rs. 15,000. Any subsequent amendment requires an additional fee of Rs. 500.

question: What is the validity of an Operational Certificate under the CG Industrial Development Policy, and how does it differ from a Production Certificate?
answer: Operational Certificate is valid for 2 years from date of issuance, while a Production Certificate's Continuity Certificate is valid for 1 year. The key difference is that the Operational Certificate is issued to manufacturing and recognized service enterprises that are ineligible for investment promotion incentives or do not wish to claim them (per Para 19(f) of Annexure-1). It can be revoked with 15 days' notice if issued based on false information or if the unit is found closed. The Operational Certificate is treated as equivalent to a Production Certificate for tenders and other departmental purposes.

question: Under the Net SGST Reimbursement Grant Rules, what types of sales are eligible for reimbursement and what is specifically excluded?
answer: Only Net SGST paid electronically through the Electronic Cash Ledger on B2C (business to final consumer within Chhattisgarh) sales is eligible. The unit must have separate GST registration and sell only B2C. Excluded: (1) Sales where the buyer has claimed Input Tax Credit; (2) Sales where the final product is used as raw material for another unit; (3) IGST on sales outside CG; (4) SGST on purchase of machines, plant & machinery, raw material; (5) Interest, penalty, and reverse charge mechanism payments under the GST Act. First claim must be submitted within 1 year of commercial production start.

question: What financial assistance is provided for SME listing on stock exchanges under the CG Industrial Development Policy?
answer: Up to 50% reimbursement of listing expenses, with a maximum subsidy of Rs. 10 lakh per unit. Applicable for listing on BSE SME Platform and NSE Emerge Platform. Eligible expenses include fees paid to SEBI, stock exchanges, merchant bankers, and other intermediaries. The company must be incorporated and have manufacturing/service operations in Chhattisgarh. This is a single-time benefit per enterprise.

question: What are the minimum warehouse storage capacity and building cost ceiling under the CG Logistics Policy 2025, and what are the Fixed Capital Investment Grant percentages for cold storage across the three block groups?
answer: Minimum warehouse storage capacity: 1,000 metric tonnes, calculated at 2 tonnes per square metre. Building cost ceiling: Rs. 1,000 per square foot. For cold storage, Fixed Capital Investment Grant: Group-1: 40% of eligible FCI, max Rs. 20 crore; Group-2: 45%, max Rs. 22 crore; Group-3: 50%, max Rs. 25 crore. Smart warehouses receive an additional 5% grant with a 5% increase in the maximum limit. Options between Net SGST and capital grant are mutually exclusive and irrevocable.

question: What are the minimum hotel key requirements for availing investment incentives in different areas of Chhattisgarh under the January 2026 policy amendment?
answer: Raipur, Bilaspur, and Durg: Five-star hotels with minimum 150 keys by an established brand. Jagdalpur and Ambikapur development blocks: Three-star hotels with minimum 100 keys. Other development blocks of Bastar/Surguja divisions: Three-star hotels with minimum 50 keys. Other development blocks (outside the above): Three-star hotels with minimum 100 keys. After the amendment, investment incentives are limited to only the first 10 hotels in each district.

question: What are the grant rates for Project Report, Quality Certification, Technical Patent, and Technology Purchase under the CG Project Report Grant Rules?
answer: Project Report Grant: 1% of FCI, max Rs. 10 lakh (startups: max Rs. 5 lakh; special category: 1.10%, max Rs. 11 lakh). Quality Certification Grant: 50% of expenditure per certification, max Rs. 10 lakh (startups: 80%, max Rs. 10 lakh; special category: 55%, max Rs. 11 lakh). Technical Patent Grant: 50% of expenditure, max Rs. 20 lakh (startups: max Rs. 10 lakh; special category: 55%, max Rs. 22 lakh). Technology Purchase Grant (from NRDC/govt research centres): 50% of expenditure, max Rs. 10 lakh (startups: max Rs. 10 lakh; special category: 55%, max Rs. 11 lakh).

question: A new pharmaceutical manufacturing unit in Chhattisgarh with plant and machinery investment of Rs. 80 crore wants to claim incentives. What enterprise category does it fall under, is it eligible for clinical trial expense reimbursement, and if it is located within 10 km of a Protected Area, what EIA clearance category applies?
answer: With plant and machinery investment of Rs. 80 crore, it qualifies as a Large Enterprise (exceeding Rs. 50 crore threshold). Pharmaceutical manufacturing at Rs. 500+ lakh investment qualifies as a Thrust Sector enterprise under Schedule-2. Yes, as a large enterprise in the pharmaceutical sector (Chapter S-1), it is eligible for clinical trial expense reimbursement with an 18-month application window and CDSCO authorization requirement. Under the EIA Notification 2006, being within 10 km of a Protected Area notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 automatically elevates any Category B project to Category A (General Condition), requiring Central Government (MoEF) review through the Expert Appraisal Committee instead of State-level SEIAA.
source_document: industrial policy _24-30_updated till 27.05.2025_hindi.pdf; Clinical_Trial_Pratipurti_Niyam (1).pdf; EIA Notification, 2006.pdf

question: A factory in Chhattisgarh employs 600 workers and handles hazardous processes listed in the First Schedule of the Factories Act. It generates 3 TPA of hazardous waste and has a Pollution Index of 85. What mandatory officers must it appoint under the Factories Act, what is its maximum hazardous waste storage period, and what is the CPCB inspection frequency?
answer: Mandatory officers with 600 workers: Safety Officer (mandatory at 500+ workers under Section 40-B); Welfare Officer (mandatory at 500+ workers under CG Factory Rules 88-91). Additionally, a canteen is mandatory (250+ under Section 46) and an ambulance room is mandatory (500+ under Section 45). A Safety Committee is also mandatory (250+ workers or factories with hazardous processes under Rule 73I). For hazardous waste of 3 TPA (less than 5 TPA), the maximum storage period is 365 days under the 2024 HWM Amendment. With a Pollution Index of 85 (PI >= 80), the factory falls in the Red category, requiring CPCB inspection at least once every 6 months and CTO validity of up to 5 years.

question: Compare the appeal fee structure across the various subsidy schemes under the CG Industrial Development Policy 2024-30. Which scheme charges no appeal fee, and what are the concessional fee categories?
answer: The Margin Money subsidy is the only scheme that charges no appeal fee at all. For other schemes, the general appeal fee structure is: Micro/Small enterprises: Rs. 2,000 (for schemes where first order is by DTIC) or Rs. 5,000 (where first order is by Industry Directorate). Medium/Large: Rs. 5,000. Concessional categories across all schemes include SC/ST, Divyang (disabled), women entrepreneurs, third gender, retired soldiers/Agniveer, and Naxal-affected persons, who pay reduced fees: Rs. 1,000 (for micro/small tier) and Rs. 2,500 (for medium/large tier). Appeals against DTIC orders go to Industry Commissioner/Director, while appeals against Industry Directorate orders go to the Principal Secretary, Commerce and Industry Department.
